jobs.name: daily-composition-methods-research
jobs.prompt:
1. Research one new music composition method (algorithmic, traditional, or AI-driven).
2. Use the 'Musical Elements Framework' (PITCH, RHYTHM, HARMONY, STRUCTURE, TEXTURE).
3. Explain how the method fills in the UnitMatrix (Voices & Sections).
4. Append the method to /opt/data/projects/Research/CompositionMethods/methods_db.md.
5. Notify Axel via Telegram with a summary of the new method.

jobs.name: MusicTech Surveillance & Replicability Analysis
jobs.prompt: Find latest music tech hardware and software gear news/reviews on https://musictech.com/, https://www.synthtopia.com/, and https://www.soundonsound.com/. Focus on technical capabilities: synthesis methods, algorithmic sequencers, MIDI patterns, DSP, spectral, or orchestration. Analyze whether I (Musicom Agent) can replicate or use them via Python, FluidSynth, Mido, custom math, or DSP. Deliver direct technical report. No filler, caveman style.

jobs.name: daily-sound-production-research
jobs.prompt:
1. Research one new sound production or audio synthesis method (physical modeling, subtractive, FM, wavetable, spectral, granular, post-processing DSP, spatialization, etc.).
2. Focus on technical mechanics, synthesis equations, and implementation requirements (Python/NumPy, FluidSynth, or VST pipelines).
3. Append the researched method to the Sound Production Methods Framework in '/opt/data/projects/Research/CompositionMethods/methods_db.md' under the 'Sound Production Methods Framework' section using the SP-XXX ID format.
4. Keep the framework table clean and formatted. Report the discovered method clearly to Axel in caveman style.

jobs.name: weekly-newsletter-digest-summarizer
jobs.prompt:
Read the output of fetch_newsletters.py script (injected below).
Identify actual weekly newsletters / digests. Strip out transactional notifications (Google setup, GitHub failed runs, etc.).
If no newsletters found, report "No newsletters found in past 7 days."
If newsletters found, summarize each newsletter. Use caveman style: short fragments, high accuracy, zero filler, no marketing speak.
Extract key signals, technical insights, or action items.
Output format:
## NEWSLETTER DIGEST

### [Newsletter Subject] - [Sender] ([Date])
- **Summary**: [Short caveman summary of core content]
- **Key Signal**: [Actionable technical pattern, insight, or announcement]

(Repeat for each)

jobs.name: daily-algorithmic-composition-production
jobs.prompt:
You are a senior Musicom algorithmic composition and sound production agent. Every day, you must autonomously create or iterate on an algorithmic music project in the 'projects/Styles/' directory.

Follow these strict steps:
1. SELECT RANDOM METHODS FROM DATABASE:
   Read `/opt/data/projects/Research/CompositionMethods/methods_db.md`.
   Extract the list of all available Composition Method IDs (e.g., 001 to 035+) and Sound Production Method IDs (e.g., SP-001 to SP-024+).
   Select one Composition Method ID and one Sound Production Method ID completely at random. Do NOT bias toward the latest additions or research outputs. Ensure a high-entropy random choice across the entire framework.

2. SELECT TARGET PROJECT:
   Inspect /opt/data/projects/Styles/. Decide to either:
   - Create a brand new project in a style folder (Fanfare, Folk, Reggae, Arabic, Experimental, Electronic). Use the next available 3-digit zero-padded ID. Copy from /opt/data/projects/Research/_TEMPLATE/.
   - Or continue an existing project to produce a new version (e.g., v2, v3).

3. COMPOSE MELODY, HARMONY, AND STRUCTURE:
   - Execute all Python generation using `/opt/data/micromamba/envs/musicom/bin/python`.
   - HARD RULE: Use the installed `musicom` engine library. Never bypass `UnitMatrixComposer`.
   - Sanctioned workflow: `create_matrix` -> `add_voice` -> `add_section` -> `fill_voice_section` -> `validate` -> `to_midi`.
   - Prevent cumulative timing drift / track desync: Collect all start/end ticks, sort note-offs before note-ons, and pad any shorter track to the exact target length.
   - Run `composer.validate()`. Assert exported .mid file size > 40 bytes.
   - Write a `provenance.json` sidecar.
   - Write a `grid_visualization.txt` of the rhythm DNA.

4. RENDER HIGH-QUALITY AUDIO:
   - Render MIDI to WAV using FluidSynth CLI: `/opt/data/micromamba/envs/musicom/bin/fluidsynth -ni -F <wav_path> -g 1.2 /usr/share/sounds/sf2/FluidR3_GM.sf2 <midi_path>` (ensure soundfont path is correct).
   - Apply peak normalization to ~-1dB via FFmpeg or Python/NumPy.
   - Compress WAV to Opus OGG: `ffmpeg -i <wav_path> -codec:a libopus -application voip -b:a 48k <ogg_path> -y`.
   - Keep only compressed .ogg and .mid. Delete intermediate raw .wav.

5. GENERATE DASHBOARD:
   - Create or update `index.html` dashboard in the project directory using VoltAgent styling (Black/Emerald theme, #050507 background, #00d992 accent, JetBrains Mono font, ASCII rhythm grid).

6. RUN COMPLIANCE PREFLIGHT:
   - Execute the preflight check: `/opt/data/micromamba/envs/musicom/bin/python /opt/data/projects/Research/preflight_check.py <your_project_dir>`
   - Ensure it returns Exit 0. Fix any violations.

7. COMMIT AND DELIVER:
   - Commit files with clear message.
   - Deliver exactly ONE audio file (.ogg) back to the Telegram chat as the primary MEDIA: item.
   - Report the details in strict, concise caveman style: high technical accuracy, no filler, short fragments. State:
     - Project folder and ID
     - Selected composition methods (e.g. Method 022) and sound production methods (e.g. SP-013)
     - Core musical DNA (pitch, rhythm, harmony, structure)
     - Key metrics and preflight status.
